messages:
ciara: deploy-bot pushed kernel v4.0 to canary at 08:17 and the prefix cache hit for /summarize-route tanked shortly after
lee: how big a hit?
ciara: from ~22.0% -> 12.4% over 30m for model rdx-llama-7B, tokens_saved down ~27k/hr on that route
aditya: that's ~44% relative hit-rate loss, ouch. any per-tenant skew?
ciara: yes: TenantAtlas 26%->13%, RetailOne 18%->9%, internal-testing 31%->28%
jamie: looks concentrated on multi-turn flows and clients that send trailing newlines in prompts
ciara: profiling shows change in batching fold logic in v4.0: scheduler now groups variable-length requests into tighter micro-batches which occasionally strips trailing empty tokens at chunk boundaries
aditya: stripping trailing tokens would change prompt fingerprint if keyer is raw-bytes based
ciara: exactly. KV lookup count didn't spike much, but miss-rate increased. KV latency flat -> key mismatch rather than store issue
ops-bot: incident created INC-2024 (P2) for kernel-rollout-cache-regression
lee: can we see a sample of delta keys? top-key share before vs after would be ideal
ciara: pulled a 10k sample. before: top-50 keys = 52% of hits. after: top-50 keys = 34%. gist: https://gists.redwood/sample-key-delta-v4.txt
jamie: that points to higher key diversity, likely fragmentation of otherwise identical prompts due to altered chunk boundaries
aditya: did the tokenizer change between models? rdx-llama-7B normalizes CRLF to LF but earlier micro-batching may have preserved CRLF in some boundaries
ciara: yes we saw a divergence: when a request boundary cut between \r and \n the serialization sometimes produced "\r" last byte vs nothing. small but enough to change fingerprint
qa-bot: reproduced locally by replaying traffic with batch folding param set to new and old. new folding shows boundary-trim events where old preserved trailing whitespace
lee: mitigation options? rollback kernel? patch keyer to canonicalize? both?
aditya: short-term: revert canary to v3.x to stabilize savings. medium: make keyer canonicalize whitespace/line-endings. long-term: batching-aware key invariants (ignore trailing whitespace tokens)
jamie: agree. cost hit if we leave v4.0: estimated +$3.1k/day on /summarize-route at current prod volumes; canary is 7% of traffic now so limited but risky on full rollout
ciara: created PR #perf-402 to guard against harmful folding heuristics and PR #key-212 to canonicalize keys. planning an A/B on canary: 50% keep v4 folding + key-normalizer, 50% v4 folding without canonicalizer
ops-bot: A/B experiment created: exp-llama-cache-aug-01
aditya: good idea. if canonicalizer restores hit-rate we can still keep kernel improvements without full revert
lee: dashboard updates requested: add panel kernel-version vs hit-rate, per-tenant token-saved waterfall, and a small panel for sample-key-entropy timeseries
ciara: dashboard link: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/prefix/summarize-route?range=2h
jamie: add alert: if route token_saved drop >15% over 1h -> page oncall and open incident automatically
aditya: also add hourly sampler job to persist N canonical prompt hashes per-tenant to diagnose churn quickly
ciara: repro snippet that shows boundary issue:
```
requests = ["Summarize the meeting notes:\n\n- item one","Summarize the meeting notes:\r\n\n- item one"]
# new folding collapses chunk boundary leaving trailing \r in second request -> different fingerprint
```
jamie: small nuance: some SDKs send trailing spaces intentionally; normalizing aggressively could mask customer intent. key-normalizer should only canonicalize harmless whitespace (CRLF->LF, trim trailing NULs) and be opt-in via feature flag per-tenant initially
aditya: agree on opt-in. we can flip for internal-testing and a few tolerant tenants first
ops-bot: rollback PR rl-412 opened to pause rollout if A/B fails
ciara: runbook draft for oncall triage:
1) check kernel-vers vs hit-rate panel and tenant waterfall
2) fetch top-100 key samples (gists) from sampler job
3) replay traffic with old/new folding params locally to confirm boundary differences
4) enable key-normalizer feature flag for the canary subset if confirmed
5) if no recovery in 4h or token_saved loss >20% persist: revert kernel rollout
aditya: timeline: run A/B for 3h, check results at 3h and 6h. rollback if no >80% recovery of lost tokens_saved at 6h
lee: can someone add a short PR test to assert that prompt hash is invariant to CRLF vs LF? that would have caught this earlier
jamie: adding unit in #key-212 to fail on regression. also adding a lightweight fuzz test in scheduler tests to ensure folding doesn't drop trailing bytes
ciara: action items: @aditya kick off A/B, @jamie update keyer PR and tests, @lee add dashboard panels & alert, @ops-bot keep incident updated
product-lead: tagging product to track savings metric drift; cc @michael for downstream billing signals
ciara: will post A/B metrics and gists back here in ~2-3h. thanks all :thumbsup:
